parsed.why: Sodomy law latent and unenforced (no prosecutions); 2015 report found no societal anti-LGBT hostility, but that is stale and the record is thin on gender identity. Third-gender tradition read positively; no documented border, facility or police exposure for trans visitors. Extrapolated, not evidenced.

Documented enforcement: 2023 mass arrests, prison sentences for homosexual acts, a death in detention, presidential call to stone people, no rule of law, no legal recognition, no protection. Hostile state framing plus generalised state violence makes outing perilous; trans-specific data absent but structure resolves low.

Working protections: gender-identity anti-discrimination, bathroom access protected, marriage equality, action plan, and a murder prosecuted with a 12-year sentence. Offset by above-regional LGBTIQ avoidance figures, absent gender-identity hate-crime law, and older social conservatism. Highest of the five.

Documented state custody exposure (birth-sex placement, isolation, strip searches; oversight findings recurring without remedy), border document friction, hostel facility dispute, and 64% of trans respondents reporting discrimination. Strong hate-crime and anti-discrimination law partially mitigates but does not remedy the documented pattern.

Universal-exposure document regime (passport markers reverted, visa refusal risk, permanent-ineligibility guidance), bathroom bans across many states with a documented trespass arrest, abusive custody practice, and allied travel advisories. Courts partly restrain it; local variation and some protections remain, so not the floor.
